jobs.title: Platform Engineer - AI Infrastructure
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Platform Engineer - AI Infrastructure

About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India’s full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India’s leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

Sarvam runs a large, multi-vendor GPU fleet that serves two demanding workloads on the same physical infrastructure: training jobs that span hundreds of GPUs, and inference services that must hold a flat p99 under production load. This role builds the platform that sits on top of that fleet - the scheduling, scaling, multi-tenancy, serving, and self-service layers that let our ML teams use thousands of GPUs without a human in the loop for every job.

This is the build side of infrastructure, not the operate side. Our SREs keep the fleet reliable and carry the pager; you build the systems that make the fleet usable - and that make it break less in the first place. The work is heavy software engineering: you will design and ship control-plane services, scheduler integrations, autoscaling controllers, the inference-serving platform, RBAC and quota systems, observability and cost tooling, and the CLI and APIs ML engineers touch every day. You will treat the platform as a product and its internal users as customers.

You should be a strong systems engineer who is fluent in Kubernetes at the controller and internals level, comfortable in Go or Python, and literate in the GPU-specific constraints - MIG and GPU sharing, gang scheduling, topology-aware placement, RDMA - that make this different from a generic cloud platform.

What You’ll Do

This is the surface area of the platform. You won't own all of it at once - you'll take a capability and build it end to end - but you should be excited by most of it.

  • The serving platform. The control plane that turns a model artifact into a scalable, multi-tenant endpoint: intelligent routing and load balancing across replicas, rollout machinery (canary, blue-green, rollback), traffic splitting, model-version integration etc.

  • The scaling and elasticity layer. Autoscaling for both training (elastic and gang scaling, scale-to-fit) and serving (queue-depth and utilization-driven), capacity pooling across clusters, burst handling, preemption and reclaim, and efficient bin-packing across GPUs etc.

  • Scheduling and orchestration. The scheduler layer itself - Kueue, Volcano, Slurm-on-Kubernetes, or custom controllers - with gang scheduling, priority and preemption, queue fairness, quota enforcement, and topology-aware placement that keeps a job's ranks on the same fabric island.

  • Multi-tenancy, RBAC, and isolation. The tenant model and namespacing, RBAC and policy, quota and fair-share enforcement, MIG / MPS / time-slicing exposed as self-service tiers, secrets and credential management, and audit logging.

  • Networking components. Platform-level network plumbing - CNI configuration and custom components, ingress and service routing, RDMA / SR-IOV exposure into pods, tenant network policy and segmentation, and multi-cluster connectivity.

  • Observability and cost tooling. The metrics, logging, and tracing pipeline as a platform feature with cardinality managed at fleet scale.

  • The storage and data path. Abstractions over the parallel filesystem, caching tiers, volume provisioning, and data-locality-aware placement.

  • Developer experience and self-service. The layer ML engineers actually touch - CLI, SDK, and APIs, job-submission abstractions and inner-loop tooling.

  • Provisioning and infrastructure-as-code. The control plane that stands clusters up reproducibly - Terraform, Crossplane, or operators; node lifecycle and image management; driver and firmware rollout automation; and multi-vendor cluster bring-up.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years building infrastructure or platform software, with a track record of systems you designed and shipped - not scripts and glue, but services and control planes that others built on.

  • Strong software engineering in Go or Python, with the judgment to build maintainable systems and the depth to debug them in production.

  • Kubernetes at the controller and internals level - you have written operators or controllers, understand the scheduler and API machinery, and know where its abstractions leak.

  • Working literacy in the GPU-specific platform constraints: MIG and GPU sharing, gang scheduling, topology- and fabric-aware placement, and why training and serving contend for the same hardware.

  • A product mindset toward internal users - you design APIs and abstractions people want to use, and you measure the platform by adoption and self-service, not by tickets closed.

  • The range to own a capability end to end, from design through rollout to the documentation that makes it self-serve.

Bonus Points

  • Having built a serving or inference or training platform - routing, autoscaling, and rollout for model endpoints at scale, fine-tuning as a service etc.

  • Experience with GPU scheduling systems (Kueue, Volcano, Slurm, Run:ai, or custom schedulers) in multi-tenant production.

  • Multi-tenant isolation (MIG, MPS, time-slicing) shipped as a self-service platform capability rather than a one-off configuration.

  • Deep Kubernetes networking - CNI internals, custom network components, or RDMA / SR-IOV in pods.

  • On-premise GPU platform work, including multi-vendor or Indian NCP environments.

  • Open-source contributions to Kubernetes, scheduling, or GPU-platform projects.

Why Sarvam?

Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population-scale impact.

Work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar

High ownership and high impact, from day one

Everything we do is AI-first, from the way we build and ship to the way we think about problems

You can work on problems that could change how an entire country learns, works, and communicates

If you want to work on problems at the frontier of AI in India, Sarvam is the place to be.

 - Deep Kubernetes networking - CNI internals, custom network components, or RDMA / SR-IOV in pods.

jobs.title: Marketing Operations Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India’s full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India’s leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

The Marketing Operations Manager makes Sarvam's marketing engine run. This role owns the systems, data, and processes that connect every campaign, channel, and team, from the website and developer signups through to pipeline and revenue. The job is to make marketing measurable: to know what is working, what is not, and where every rupee and hour is going. This person sits at the centre of a fast-moving marketing team spanning growth, demand generation, product marketing, and developer relations. They build the martech stack, keep the data clean, run attribution, and turn a lean team into a leveraged one by automating the manual and instrumenting the unmeasured.

What You’ll Do

  • Martech stack ownership. Own selection, integration, and administration of the marketing stack - CRM, marketing automation, analytics, attribution, and enrichment tools. Keep systems connected and data flowing cleanly between them.

  • Funnel instrumentation. Instrument the full funnel from first visit and developer signup through to MQL, SQL, and closed revenue. Define the stages, the data model, and the definitions everyone agrees on.

  • Attribution & reporting. Build and maintain attribution models and reporting that show what drives pipeline and usage. Deliver dashboards leadership actually uses to make decisions.

  • Lead management & routing. Own lead scoring, routing, and the MQL-to-SQL handoff with Sales, with clear SLAs on quality and follow-up. Keep the bridge between Marketing and Sales clean and accountable.

  • Campaign operations. Set up, QA, and support campaign execution across email, paid, events, and lifecycle. Build the templates, workflows, and processes so campaigns ship faster with fewer errors.

  • Data hygiene & governance. Keep the database accurate, deduplicated, and compliant. Own segmentation, list management, and data governance including consent and privacy requirements.

  • Process & enablement. Document workflows, build playbooks, and train the team on the systems. Remove the manual, repetitive work that slows the team down.

  • AI-native workflows. Use AI to compress every operational cycle — reporting, QA, enrichment, segmentation, and content ops. Treat the ops function itself as a place to apply Sarvam's own tools.

  • Budget & vendor management. Track marketing spend against pipeline, manage tool contracts and renewals, and surface where budget is and is not paying off.

What We're Looking For

  • 4-6 years in marketing operations, revenue operations, or a closely related role at a B2B technology or SaaS company

  • Hands-on expertise with at least one major marketing automation platform (HubSpot, Marketo, or similar) and a CRM (Salesforce or similar), including building workflows, scoring, and integrations yourself

  • Strong analytical capability - you build your own dashboards, define attribution, and pull and model your own data

  • Track record of designing and improving lead management, funnel instrumentation, and Marketing-to-Sales handoff processe

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India’s full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India’s leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

Sarvam is looking for a Business Development Representative to drive outbound prospecting, engage decision-makers, and generate qualified pipeline. In this role you will run cold calls, email, and LinkedIn outreach to identify and nurture new business opportunities, and partner closely with Account Executives to turn interest into qualified meetings. A working grasp of the Sarvam stack will let you translate complex AI concepts into clear value for enterprise teams, and strong messaging instincts will help you reach the right decision-makers with outreach that lands.

What You’ll Do

  • Prospect and qualify. Build a steady pipeline of high-potential opportunities through cold calls, email, and social outreach.

  • Engage decision-makers. Reach out to enterprise prospects, understand their pain points, and position Sarvam's solutions as effective, scalable answers.

  • Run discovery. Conduct initial discovery calls to assess needs, qualify fit, and guide prospects into the evaluation process.

  • Partner with Account Executives. Align on target accounts, prioritise outreach, and hand off qualified opportunities cleanly to accelerate pipeline growth.

  • Keep the CRM clean. Maintain accurate records of every interaction, track activity and trends, and surface insights for continuous improvement.

  • Work with Marketing. Partner on outreach strategy, share what is landing with prospects, and help refine messaging and campaigns for higher engagement.

  • Hit your targets. Own and consistently meet activity and qualified-meeting targets that feed the pipeline.

What We're Looking For

  • 3-5 years of experience, including at least 2 years in a SaaS-based BDR/SDR role, demonstrating strong sales acumen.

  • Proven track record of successfully cold-calling and converting enterprise decision-makers into high-value business opportunities.

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to engage prospects, build rapport, and foster long-term client relationships.

jobs.title: Head of Brand & Communications
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India’s full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India’s leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

Sarvam is building sovereign AI for India - foundational models, a developer platform, and enterprise products that put AI to work across BFSI, healthcare, and the public sector. The Head of Brand & Communications owns how that story is understood: how Sarvam shows up to developers, enterprises, the media, policymakers, and the public, and how a coherent brand and narrative are built across every channel.

The mandate is to define Sarvam's brand and lead its communications — shaping press narratives, driving proactive media engagement, placing the founders and research where they matter, and building credibility with technical, business, and policy audiences. You will set the strategy and build the system: the brand identity, the narrative, the newsroom, and the team and partners to execute across earned, owned, and social channels.

You will serve as a strategic advisor to senior leadership and the founders, and play a critical role in ensuring communications is not a service function but a driver of business outcomes — pipeline, adoption, talent, and trust.

What You’ll Do

  • Brand strategy & identity. Own Sarvam's brand end-to-end — positioning, narrative, voice, and visual identity — and keep it coherent across product, marketing, recruiting, and public moments as the company scales.

  • Press & media engagement. Own the press narrative. Build and maintain strong relationships with top-tier business, technology, and trade press in India and globally, and proactively drive coverage that advances Sarvam's positioning.

  • Narrative & messaging. Translate complex models, platform capabilities, and research into clear, credible narratives that resonate with developers, technical buyers, executives, and policymakers — without diluting the technical depth.

  • Founder & executive visibility. Place Sarvam's founders and research in the rooms that matter — AI summits, policy circles, global benchmarks, and tier-1 media. Prepare leaders to be effective spokespeople across press, podcasts, panels, and stage.

  • Thought leadership & policy comms. Shape Sarvam's voice on sovereign AI, India's AI stack, and the policy conversations the company is part of. Produce POVs, briefings, and narratives that establish category leadership.

  • Product & launch communications. Lead comms for every model and product release — from launch narrative to the steady cadence of capability releases and developer-facing news. Know which moments deserve the spotlight and which don't.

  • Integrated marcomms. Partner closely with Marketing, Product, Developer Relations, and Sales to co-develop integrated campaigns and storytelling that span earned, owned, and social channels in a single coordinated voice.

  • Owned & social channels. Own Sarvam's owned newsroom, blog, and social presence. Drive proactive storytelling that increases the volume and consistency of high-quality narratives about Sarvam's impact.

  • Customer & ecosystem storytelling. Partner with GTM teams and customers to bring real-world use cases and impact to life across industries and regions, turning adoption into credible, repeatable stories.

  • Crisis & issues management. Exercise sound judgment in high-velocity, high-scrutiny moments — prioritise, triage, and lead the company's response through ambiguity.

  • Build & scale the function. Hire, structure, and develop the brand and communications team, and bring in agencies or partners for social, content, design, and programmatic execution where needed.

What We're Looking For

  • 12+ years in communications, brand, or marketing, with deep expertise leading communications in high-growth technology environments

  • Strong press instincts and relationships, with a track record of shaping narratives and landing impactful coverage with business, technology, and industry media

  • Demonstrated ability to operate as a strategic advisor to founders and senior executives — not just an executor of comms plans

  • Experience building and owning a brand — positioning, narrative, voice, and identity — and keeping it coherent as a company scales

  • Experience engaging technical and enterprise stakeholders — developers, CIOs, CTOs, and line-of-business leaders — with the ability to tailor messaging across segments

  • Experience working in highly cross-functional, matrixed organisations, with strong instincts for alignment across product, GTM, and marketing

  • Ability to build and scale teams, including structuring complementary capabilities such as social, content, and design under a broader comms strategy

  • Sound judgment in high-scrutiny environments, with a balance of strategic thinking and a strong bias to action and measurable impact

Bonus Points

  • Existing relationships with reporters, analysts, and editors covering AI, enterprise tech, and the Indian technology ecosystem

jobs.title: Head of Data Operations
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Role

Sarvam AI is building India's sovereign full-stack Generative AI platform - foundational models and AI solutions that understand Indian languages, culture, and diversity. High-quality data is the fuel behind this mission, and we're looking for a detail-oriented deal maker to own data procurement end-to-end: from understanding what our Models team needs, to sourcing it from the right providers, to closing deals, to ensuring the data actually lands and meets the bar.

This is a high-ownership, high-accountability role at the intersection of operations, vendor management, and applied AI - ideal for someone who thrives on structure, negotiation, and getting things done right the first time.

What You'll Do

  • Translate requirements into action: Work closely with the Models team to understand data requirements - languages, formats, volumes, quality benchmarks and convert them into clear sourcing briefs.

  • Source and negotiate: Identify, evaluate, and negotiate with data providers and vendors to secure high-quality data at the right cost and timeline.

  • Own the full deal lifecycle: Drive every deal from proposal through to closure : contracts, pricing, timelines, and terms with rigor and attention to detail.

  • Manage data exchange: Coordinate the secure and timely exchange of data between providers and internal teams, ensuring nothing falls through the cracks.

  • Close the feedback loop: Collect and relay quality feedback from the Models team back to providers, ensuring continuous improvement in data quality and holding vendors accountable to standards.

  • Build ops rigor: Establish and maintain strong operational controls and tracking systems across the entire procurement lifecycle: proposal, negotiation, contracting, delivery, and feedback so nothing is ambiguous or untracked.

  • Manage multiple deals in parallel: Juggle several provider relationships and deals simultaneously without compromising on quality or timelines.

What We're Looking For

  • 8+ years of overall experience, including 2–3 years in data procurement, vendor management, sourcing, or a similar deal-making/operations role: ideally involving data, content, or similar structured deliverables.

  • A detail-oriented operator who can hold multiple moving pieces (deals, timelines, quality bars) without losing precision.

  • Strong negotiation and deal-closing instincts- comfortable working directly with external vendors and providers to land favorable terms.

  • Proven ability to build and run process and operational controls- you don't just get the deal done, you make sure it's trackable and repeatable.

  • Comfortable working cross-functionally with technical teams (Models/Research) and translating their needs into vendor-facing requirements.

  • Strong communication and follow-through able to close the loop with both providers and internal stakeholders.

  • Bias for ownership: you treat data procurement as your business, not a checklist.

Why Join Sarvam AI

  • Be part of a small, high-caliber team building India's sovereign Generative AI stack from the ground up.

  • Work at the intersection of cutting-edge AI research and real-world operational execution.

  • High-visibility role with direct impact on the quality and pace of our model development.

  • Work directly with the founding team and Head of Operations in a fast-moving, mission-driven environment.

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India’s full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India’s leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

We’re looking for an FDE to work directly with enterprise clients integrating our platform into their business workflows. You will be embedded with clients - understanding their operational processes, configuring the platform for their needs, debugging issues end-to-end, and ensuring they achieve high-quality outcomes across their use cases.

This is a hands-on, client-facing engineering role. You’ll split time between writing code (integration scripts, platform configuration, bug fixes) and working directly with client engineering and business teams. You’ll develop deep expertise in the platform and become the trusted technical point of contact for your accounts.

What you'll do

  • Own the technical arc of customer engagements, from scoping the solution through to the system running in production.

  • Design end-to-end AI systems that meet real reliability, latency, accuracy, and cost constraints. Make the architectural decisions that hold up at production scale.

  • Build the system yourself, across whatever the stack and product call for. Engagements range from voice and conversational systems at enterprise customers, to developer tooling around Sarvam's APIs, to translation and dubbing pipelines for media customers, to agentic workflows and the MCP servers and infrastructure that underpin them. FDSEs are hands-on engineers, not technical project managers.

  • Deploy into the customer's environment, working closely with their engineering team on data, infrastructure, and integration constraints.

  • Set up evaluations that meaningfully measure whether the system is doing its job, and iterate based on what the data shows.

  • Work across engagements over time, picking up new domains, products, and customer contexts as priorities shift.

  • Bring what you learn in the field back to Sarvam's product and research teams, and shape what gets built next.

Who we're looking for

We're hiring across levels, 4+ years of experience would be preferred. Strong AI fundamentals, range across the stack, high agency, and a clear track record of shipping matter more than years of experience. We're looking for engineers with a technical degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent.

  • High agency. You unblock yourself. You don't wait for direction. When a customer is stuck or an engagement is ambiguous, you figure out what to do next and do it.

  • Strong AI fundamentals. You deeply understand how LLMs and agents work in production: context engineering, memory, RAG, tool use, structured outputs, and the failure modes that actually show up at scale. You've worked with agentic frameworks (LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Google ADK, or equivalent) and with both open and closed source models.

  • Evals mindset. You know how to evaluate agentic AI systems. You can set up eval pipelines, define metrics that matter for a given use case, and have clear opinions on what good evaluation looks like versus what's just noise.

  • Systems thinker. You can reason about architecture, reliability, scale, trade-offs, and failure modes across services, databases, queues, and messaging systems (Kafka, SQS, or equivalent). You make design decisions that hold up at production load, not just in a notebook.

  • Range, and the ability to pick things up fast. Strong Python, comfortable across backend, data pipelines, and cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or equivalent). You can be useful on a voice agent, a backend service, an evaluation harness, or a developer-facing integration. When you don't know a stack, you pick it up in hours, not weeks.

  • Builder who stays current. You ship. You have things on the internet, in production, in open source, or in personal projects, that prove it. You follow the frontier closely, try new tools as they launch, and have strong opinions on what's actually useful versus hype.

  • Customer instinct. You can sit in a room with a customer's engineering team, understand what they actually need, and translate that into clean technical work. You communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Even better if

  • You've built and deployed AI agents into production, where they did real work for real users.

  • You have experience deploying AI systems in regulated environments (BFSI, public sector) or with on-premise / VPC deployments.

  • You have a history of side projects, open source contributions, or shipped products.

  • You've worked in a customer-facing or product-embedded engineering role before.

  • You've used Sarvam's models or APIs in your own projects.

Why Sarvam?

Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population-scale impact.

  • Work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar

  • High ownership and high impact, from day one

  • Everything we do is AI-first, from the way we build and ship to the way we think about problems

  • You can work on problems that could change how an entire country learns, works, and communicates

If you want to work on problems at the frontier of AI in India, Sarvam is the place to be.

jobs.title: Product Manager – Media & Entertainment, Sarvam Studio
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Product · Bengaluru · Full Time · On-Site

About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India's full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

Sarvam Studio is our media platform — spanning AI dubbing, live translation, text-to-speech, speech-to-text, and audiobook & podcast generation, powered by a shared foundation of voice cloning, stem separation and music generation. Its users range from individual creators to media houses to large broadcasters and streaming platforms.

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager who knows the media and entertainment industry from the inside — someone who has built products for OTT, broadcast, streaming, or media-tech platforms and understands how content actually gets made, localized, distributed, and monetized. You'll own how Studio serves the media industry: what a dubbing pipeline needs to look like for a broadcaster running hundreds of hours of content a month, what "broadcast quality" means for AI-generated voice, and how AI reshapes the economics of content creation and localization.

This is a builder's role, not a strategy-deck role. You'll talk to studios, broadcasters, and creators constantly, ship product every week, and get deep into how our voice and media models behave in production.

What You'll Do

  • Own the Studio product roadmap for media & entertainment customers end-to-end — from discovery with broadcasters, OTT platforms, and content studios, to specs, shipping, and measuring outcomes

  • Translate media workflows into product: content ingestion, dubbing and localization pipelines, QC and human-in-the-loop review, delivery formats, and rights/compliance requirements that broadcast and streaming customers demand

  • Define what "good" means for AI-generated media — voice quality, lip-sync, emotional nuance, translation fidelity — and build the eval pipelines and feedback loops that hold the product to it

  • Get into the details of how AI systems behave in production: model selection, prompt and pipeline design, latency and cost budgets, failure modes

  • Work with the GTM team on pricing, packaging, and positioning for media segments — from per-minute creator pricing to enterprise localization contracts

  • Be the voice of the media customer internally: relay precise product and model feedback (dubbing failures, audio artefacts, translation misses) to research, and close the loop with customers

  • Track the AI-in-media landscape — content creation, localization, and playout platforms — and bring a sharp point of view on where Studio should build, partner, or pass

  • Ship product every week, not plans

What We're Looking For

  • 5–10 years of product management experience, with real products shipped at meaningful scale

  • Strong preference for experience in media & entertainment — Video & Content first platforms OTT/streaming platforms (Prime Video, JioHotstar, Zee5, SonyLIV), broadcasters, studios, or media-tech/content-supply-chain companies (Adobe, Amagi, Prime Focus, or similar)

  • Deep understanding of the content lifecycle: how content is produced, transformed (dubbing, subtitling), packaged, distributed, and monetized across broadcast and streaming

  • Hands-on familiarity with generative AI in content workflows — voice synthesis, dubbing, video/audio generation — and clear thinking on quality vs. cost vs. speed trade-offs

  • Strong data skills: comfortable writing SQL, setting up funnels, and defining success metrics that matter (not vanity numbers)

  • Strong product thinking: you start with the customer's problem, structure vague problem spaces, and ship v1 without over-engineering

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Job Title: HR Business Partner (HRBP) & People Ops

 

Location: Bengaluru
Employment Type: Fulltime

About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India's full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

We're looking for an HR Business Partner & Operations to be a strategic and hands-on partner to our business leaders. You'll sit at the intersection of people strategy and execution : shaping how teams are structured, how performance and culture are managed, and making sure the operational backbone of HR (systems, policies, processes, compliance, data) runs without friction. This is a high-ownership role suited to someone who can move fluidly between advising leadership on organizational decisions and getting into the details of HR operations and systems to make those decisions real.

Key Responsibilities

Business Partnering

  • Partner closely with business and function leaders to understand their goals and translate them into HR strategies and structures that support scale.

  • Advise on organizational design, performance management, and career development as teams grow.

  • Act as a trusted advisor and change agent through periods of organizational transformation and rapid growth.

  • Address employee relations matters, lead investigations where needed, and resolve conflicts fairly and swiftly.

People Operations & HR Systems

  • Own and continuously improve core HR processes across the employee lifecycle — onboarding, performance cycles, transfers, and exits.

  • Identify, evaluate, and implement HRMS tools for employee data, compensation, and performance management, ensuring the stack scales cleanly with headcount growth.

  • Ensure HR policies, labor law compliance, and documentation are current, consistent, and audit-ready.

  • Support compensation and benefits administration, including data accuracy, benchmarking inputs, and cycle execution.

  • Maintain and improve HR systems, dashboards, and reporting to give leadership clean, timely people data.

  • Support talent acquisition through workforce planning inputs and candidate evaluation where needed.

Culture & Engagement

  • Drive employee engagement, retention, and development initiatives that fit a fast paced, high-growth, tech-first environment.

  • Champion a high performance, high trust culture aligned with Sarvam's mission and pace.

Requirements

  • Degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field.

  • 5–8 years of HR experience, with at least 4 years in an HRBP, People Operations, or similar generalist role.

  • Hands-on experience in implementing HRMS/HRIS platforms (e.g., Darwinbox, Keka, Rippling, Lattice or similar) is strongly preferred.

  • Strong grounding in HR compliance, and process design.

  • Comfortable owning both strategic conversations with leaders and the operational details that make HR systems and processes work reliably.

  • Strong stakeholder management, communication, and problem-solving skills.

  • Thrives in a fast paced, high growth, ambiguity tolerant environment: startup or scale-up experience is a plus.

Why Sarvam?

  • Sarvam is a fast moving, high talent density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population scale impact.

  • Work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar.

  • High impact, high agency role shaping HR strategy and systems from the ground up at a fast scaling AI company.

  • Be part of a mission driven team building India's sovereign AI stack, with exposure to a wide range of HR challenges, from strategy to systems.

 

If you’re passionate about shaping the people agenda in a mission first, cutting edge AI company, we’d love to hear from you!
